classification.difficultyReason: Identify right triangles within the prism, calculate base diagonals and reuse them with the vertical height for lengths and angles. Earlier parts supply the intermediate lengths needed by later parts.

content.prompt: In the rectangular prism shown, find:

spec.description: Unshaded rectangular prism with front face DCNP and rear face ABML, displaced upwards and right. AL, LM and LP are hidden dashed edges. Q is the marked midpoint of PN, with matching single ticks on PQ and QN. Ordinary source blue edges, red hidden edges and red point are rendered in house black; dashes and the filled point retain their meanings.
spec.mathematics: PN=12 cm, NM=10 cm, BM=8 cm; Q is the midpoint of PN. Corresponding depth edges are DA, CB, NM and PL. All faces are rectangles.
spec.answerVisibility: Only original vertex labels, three dimensions, midpoint ticks and the point Q are supplied; requested diagonals and answers are absent.

answer.worked:
In right-angled triangle $BMN$:
$$\begin{align*}\tan\angle BNM&=\frac{BM}{MN}\\\tan\angle BNM&=\frac{8}{10}\\\angle BNM&=\tan^{-1}\left(\frac{8}{10}\right)\\\angle BNM&\approx38.7^\circ.\end{align*}$$

answer.short:
$2\sqrt{77}\text{ cm}$

Find the base diagonal $PM$, then apply Pythagoras in $BMP$.
answer.worked:
In right-angled triangle $PNM$:
$$\begin{align*}PM^2&=PN^2+NM^2\\PM^2&=12^2+10^2\\PM^2&=244.\end{align*}$$
Since $BM$ is perpendicular to the base, triangle $BMP$ is right-angled at $M$:
$$\begin{align*}BP^2&=BM^2+PM^2\\BP^2&=8^2+244\\BP^2&=308\\BP&=2\sqrt{77}\text{ cm}.\end{align*}$$

children.prompt: the angle $BPM$ (correct to one decimal place)

answer.worked:
From part c, $PM=\sqrt{244}=2\sqrt{61}\text{ cm}$. In right-angled triangle $BMP$:
$$\begin{align*}\tan\angle BPM&=\frac{BM}{PM}\\\tan\angle BPM&=\frac{8}{2\sqrt{61}}\\\angle BPM&=\tan^{-1}\left(\frac{8}{2\sqrt{61}}\right)\\\angle BPM&\approx27.1^\circ.\end{align*}$$

$Q$ is the midpoint of $PN$, so $QN=12\div2=6\text{ cm}$. In right-angled triangle $QNM$:
$$\begin{align*}MQ^2&=QN^2+NM^2\\MQ^2&=6^2+10^2\\MQ^2&=136\\MQ&=2\sqrt{34}\text{ cm}.\end{align*}$$

children.prompt: the angle $BQM$ (correct to one decimal place)

answer.worked:
$BM$ is perpendicular to the base, so triangle $BMQ$ is right-angled at $M$. Using $MQ=2\sqrt{34}\text{ cm}$:
$$\begin{align*}\tan\angle BQM&=\frac{BM}{MQ}\\\tan\angle BQM&=\frac{8}{2\sqrt{34}}\\\angle BQM&=\tan^{-1}\left(\frac{8}{2\sqrt{34}}\right)\\\angle BQM&\approx34.4^\circ.\end{align*}$$
